    The free covering of a quiver #

    For a finite quiver Q let G = FreeGroup Q₁. The quiver Q̃ has vertices (h, v) with h ∈ G, v ∈ Q₀, and an arrow (h, a) : (h, s(a)) → (h·a, t(a)) for each arrow a of Q. The group G acts freely by left multiplication on the first coordinate, its orbits are the fibres of (h, v) ↦ v, and equally labelled arrows are translates. A finite set S of vertices of Q̃ spans a finite full subquiver D_S with a locally injective map p_S : D_S → Q, and the action gives covering data (FreeCover.coverData). G is torsion-free.
